title: Emotion regulation success involves systematic gradient-based reconfigurations of large-scale activation patterns in the human brain
experiments_summary:
The study analyzed two large fMRI datasets: a discovery sample (DS, n=358) and a replication sample (RS, n=263). Participants performed a standard cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation task with 'Look' (passive viewing of negative images) and 'Regulate' (active reappraisal) conditions, followed by emotional state ratings after each trial. Regulatory success was operationalized as the difference in mean emotional ratings between Regulate and Look conditions, z-normalized within each study.

For neural analyses, whole-brain GLM-derived, unthresholded contrast images (Look > Baseline; Regulate > Baseline) were computed per participant. These activation maps were projected into gradient space by computing Pearson correlations (Fisher Z-transformed) between each participant's condition-specific whole-brain activation map and five principal gradient maps independently derived from resting-state fMRI data in the Human Connectome Project (HCP). Regulation-related gradient shifts (ΔG1–ΔG5) were calculated as difference scores (Regulate minus Look projections) per gradient per participant.

Linear mixed models (LMMs) were used to examine whether ΔG1–ΔG5 predicted individual differences in regulatory success, controlling for emotional reactivity, age, sex, and study ID as a random effect, separately in DS and RS. Predictive validity was assessed via leave-one-participant-out cross-validation within each sample, and cross-sample generalization was tested by training on DS and predicting in RS, with statistical significance evaluated via permutation tests (5,000 iterations) with Bonferroni correction.

A supplemental group-level GLM was run with ΔG1 as a covariate for the Regulate > Look contrast across the joint sample (n=619), thresholded at p<0.001 uncorrected / FWE cluster-corrected p<0.05. A separate group-level GLM used individual regulatory success scores as a covariate for the Regulate > Look contrast to derive an unthresholded covariate t-map. Meta-analytic decoding using Neurosynth (via NiMARE) was applied to this t-map and the canonical Gradient 1 map to identify associated cognitive terms.

For ecological validity, a subset of RS participants (n=55) completed a 1-week smartphone-based experience sampling protocol (five prompts/day, 1–5 affect ratings), and a modified LMM tested whether ΔG1–ΔG5 predicted average daily affect.

Specificity analyses examined whether gradient shifts predicted ERQ-assessed habitual reappraisal and suppression scores using modified LMMs. Post-hoc analyses tested nested LMMs with all possible interaction terms among ΔG1–ΔG5, evaluated by AIC. Models using Euclidean distance (ED) between Look and Regulate in five-dimensional and three-dimensional gradient spaces were also compared via AIC. Region-wise analyses extracted gradient shifts from Schaefer-400 cortical parcels and 14 Harvard-Oxford subcortical regions and estimated region-specific LMMs predicting regulatory success, with FDR correction applied separately for cortical and subcortical regions.
